rationale.usefulness: Keeping a real harness in the training loop is useful for developers with measurable agent tasks. The report connects the documented coding recipe to controlled app repair and explains rewards, logging and failure inspection. A100/B200 examples, Kubernetes and RL expertise make this considerably less immediately actionable for ordinary educators or creative builders.
rationale.impact: Harness-aware training addresses a consequential mismatch between training and deployed agents, and the reported 41.8 to 56.4 SWE-bench Verified result provides a concrete domain signal. It remains one author-run coding setup with no full methodology audit or reproduction here; benefits across tutoring and creative production are proposed rather than demonstrated.
rationale.novelty: The deploy-time harness, model-call proxy and associated treatment of variable trajectories provide a meaningful systems differentiation. It builds on existing RL, verl and vLLM rather than introducing reinforcement learning itself, and the evidence does not establish that all architectural components are unique.
rationale.maturity: Versioned stable documentation, an executable-looking quick start and a detailed distributed coding recipe support a usable research framework. Tightly coupled GPU dependencies, substantial operations, logging defaults and reward-hacking controls are material readiness limits; no training run was reproduced.
rationale.openness: MIT framework code, inspectable components, example configurations and described data preparation offer strong inspection and adaptation rights. The score is below exceptional because reproduction needs costly infrastructure and the terms/completeness of model, dataset, image and service dependencies were not comprehensively established.

concerns: No blocking discrepancy found. August release history, October blog publication and baseline status are appropriately separated.
Default Weights & Biases trajectory upload and distinct stack licenses are important deployment constraints already disclosed. The headline result remains publisher-reported.
